title: Body Lock Passing Position
description: The top player locks low around the Guard player’s hips with chest-to-hip connection to clear the Knee Line.
topPlayerGoals: The top player wants to control Body Lock Passing Position through Head Position, Inside Position, and directed pressure.
Lock the hips, kill the hook, and clear the Knee Line layer by layer.
Keep a stable base so you are not off-balanced or countered.
bottomPlayerGoals: The bottom player wants to survive Body Lock Passing Position with frames, Pummeling, or the right angle.
Pummel the inside knee, create a shin frame, or use a shoulder crunch.
Recognize danger signals early instead of waiting for the position to settle.
controlPoints: Main control point: Low grip, head offset, and chest-to-hip connection.
Head, hands, hips, and knees should share the same force direction.
The Elbow-Knee Connection or hip-shoulder line determines whether the position is still alive or already locked.
escapePriorities: Escape priority: Create a shin or knee wedge between the chest and hips.
Protect the neck, back, Knee Line, or arm line before countering.
If Inside Position is lost, reset one defensive layer first.

advancementOptions.action: Clear the Knee Line and stabilize Side Control
advancementOptions.why: This is the natural branch when you win the main control point and the opponent is forced to defend.

dangerSignals: The chin or neck is pulled out of a safe line.
The elbow separates from the ribs or knee.
The hip line is locked while the shoulder line is still being pulled.
You need a long hand post to avoid falling.
